questions.q: How does a Bicep template call a separate, reusable .bicep file?
options: With a `required_providers` block, the same as a Terraform provider
With the `module` keyword, pointing at the other file's path
Bicep has no concept of calling one file from another
By copying the other file's resource blocks directly inline
questions.explain: module network 'modules/network.bicep' = { ... } calls a separate .bicep file as a nested deployment, the same reusability idea as a Terraform module.

questions.q: How does a caller read a value back out of a Bicep module, such as a virtual network's resource ID?
options: `<moduleName>.outputs.<outputName>`, e.g. network.outputs.vnetId
Through an environment variable set by the CLI
By declaring the same resource again in the caller
It can't — module outputs are not readable from the calling template
questions.explain: A module's output block exposes a value, and the caller reads it as network.outputs.vnetId, mirroring how a Terraform module's output is referenced.

questions.q: What does the `using 'main.bicep'` statement at the top of a .bicepparam file do?
options: Imports every resource from main.bicep into the parameter file
Is purely a comment with no functional effect
Tells Azure which resource group to deploy into
Ties the parameter file to one specific template, so values are checked against that template's parameter types at compile time
questions.explain: The using statement is what lets Bicep catch a typo'd parameter name or wrong type in a .bicepparam file before deployment, because it's checked against that exact template.

questions.q: What is a key difference between a .bicepparam file and the older JSON parameter file format?
options: .bicepparam files cannot be used with az deployment group create
JSON parameter files can only be used with ARM templates, never with Bicep
A .bicepparam file is typed and checked against its template's parameter types; the JSON format is not
There is no real difference between the two formats
questions.explain: The using statement ties a .bicepparam file to a specific template for type checking, which the older, untyped JSON parameter file format does not provide.

questions.q: In `module network 'modules/network.bicep' = { name: 'networkDeployment' ... }`, what does `name: 'networkDeployment'` actually refer to?
options: The name of the virtual network resource being created
A required alias for the .bicep file itself
The name of the resource group the module deploys into
The name of the inner nested deployment Bicep creates for that module call, visible in the Azure Portal's deployment history
questions.explain: The name on a module block names the nested deployment, not any Azure resource created inside it — the virtual network's own name comes from the vnetName parameter.
